note: Which source each set in searched.json was run against, so that the flat `searched` list Record Atlas imports can be DERIVED from `sets` rather than written twice. A set is listed here by its title (g) and date (d). `src` names the one source the whole set was run against — the provider's own name as Record Atlas writes it, or the real name where Atlas has no provider yet. `skip` says why a set contributes no flat rows: `not-a-search` (an audit, a reading of this archive's own files, an answer received) or `source-not-named` (the title does not name ONE source, and the rows do not either, so none is guessed). Nothing is inferred from the rows' wording. tools/searched_flat.py derives the rows and fails the build if a set has no entry here or if the committed flat rows differ from what this map derives.
